turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm Daniel, a software engineer in Lisbon. I just accepted an offer from Brennwerk GmbH in Munich. My partner Sofia and our daughter Lia, who's 8, are coming too, and we want to be settled before the German school year starts in September. Where do we even begin?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations! A family move to Munich has six moving parts that depend on each other: your work permit, housing, the city registration (Anmeldung) and a bank account, a school for Lia, health insurance, and shipping your things. We'll track each thread, since they interlock.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Brennwerk wants me to start on 1 July.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: 1 July gives about twelve weeks for the permit and a first place to live, which is doable. We'll plan backwards from that date.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: First, the work permit. I'm Brazilian-born with only a Brazilian passport, so I do need one. Which permit should I apply for?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: As a non-EU citizen with a university degree and a skilled job offer, the EU Blue Card is usually the best route: faster, and better family rights than a general work visa.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I qualify on salary?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The Blue Card needs a salary above a threshold that's adjusted every year, around €48,000 in 2025. Your offer of €72,000 is comfortably above it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then the Blue Card it is.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good. Brennwerk's HR can request a pre-approval from the Federal Employment Agency, which speeds things up.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What about Sofia? She's also Brazilian. She's a UX designer at a Lisbon agency and wants to keep that job, working remotely from Munich. Is she allowed to work in Germany?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good question, and the answer depends on the permit she gets as your family member. Let's check the family rules before she plans on it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Housing next. Where should we live in Munich?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Munich is expensive and competitive, so let's first set a budget, then compare neighbourhoods by commute, schools and rent.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We can spend at most €2,300 a month, warm.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: €2,300 warm (including heating and utilities) for a family flat in Munich is tight but possible outside the most central areas.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Which neighbourhoods fit that?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Pasing is cheaper and has a fast S-Bahn to the centre; Haidhausen is more central and walkable but pricier. Brennwerk's office is in the east, near Haidhausen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Pasing, then. It fits the budget.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Pasing it is. The S-Bahn commute to the east side is about 35 minutes.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Anything special about renting in Munich as foreigners?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Landlords usually ask for a credit record (SCHUFA). You won't have one yet, so bring your employment contract, recent payslips and a Portuguese bank reference instead.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: People keep mentioning the Anmeldung. What is it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The Anmeldung is the mandatory registration of your address with the city, within two weeks of moving in. Almost everything else in Germany, from bank accounts to your tax ID, depends on it.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'll open an N26 account before we arrive, so we have a German IBAN from day one.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: N26 lets you open an account online before you move, which is handy for salary and everyday spending.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What do I need for the Anmeldung itself?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Your passport and a Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, a form your landlord signs confirming you moved in. So you can only register once you actually have a flat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Lia's school: should she go to a public Grundschule or an international school?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Both are realistic in Munich; let's look at the trade-offs.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How does a public Grundschule work?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Free, and assigned by address: each address belongs to one school's catchment area, so where you live decides which Grundschule Lia attends.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the international option?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The Bavarian International School is the best known. Teaching is in English, but fees are around €18,000 a year.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Lia doesn't speak any German. Is a Grundschule even possible?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes. Munich schools have German-support programmes for newly arrived children, and eight-year-olds pick up the language fast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Health insurance: public or private?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: With a family and one main earner, public insurance is usually better: your spouse and children can be co-insured for free, whereas private insurance charges per person.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then public, with Techniker Krankenkasse, and Sofia and Lia co-insured on my policy.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: TK is a good choice with English-language service. Sofia and Lia are co-insured through your membership.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Back to the visa: the earliest appointment at the KVR, Munich's immigration office, is 8 July.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a week after your planned start date. The Blue Card itself is issued at that appointment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I start working before I have the card?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Possibly, depending on the entry visa. Let's check what the pre-approval allows.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What did you find?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: With the pre-approval and a Blue Card entry visa, you may start working before the KVR appointment. And for Sofia: as the spouse of a Blue Card holder, she gets a residence permit with unrestricted work rights, so she can work in Germany, for a German or a foreign employer.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Housing update: finding a Pasing flat from Lisbon is impossible, so we found a temporary furnished flat from 1 July instead.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Sensible: a furnished flat lets you search in person, and you can register your address there.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The catch: it's only available until 31 July.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: So you need a permanent lease starting by 1 August. That's the real deadline for the flat search.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Good news: Brennwerk offers a €300 a month relocation allowance for the first year.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's real money in the Munich rental market.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So we can raise the rent cap?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes: with the allowance, raise the cap to €2,600 warm.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: With €2,600 we could afford Haidhausen after all. It's walkable to Lia's future school and my commute would be 15 minutes. Should we switch from Pasing?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes, switch to Haidhausen: a 15-minute commute instead of 35, and a walkable school, are worth the extra rent now that it's within budget.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Does living in Haidhausen change which school Lia would go to?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Yes: the catchment rules [N_16] mean the address decides the Grundschule, so a Haidhausen address gives you a Haidhausen school.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Landlords in Haidhausen want the deposit in a rent-deposit account, a Mietkautionskonto.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's standard: the deposit, up to three months' cold rent, is held in a special blocked account.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can my N26 account do that?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Let's check: not every bank offers deposit accounts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: No: N26 doesn't offer rent-deposit accounts, and many landlords won't accept its alternatives. Open a Sparkasse account after the Anmeldung for the deposit and rent, and keep N26 only for everyday spending.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So what order do things have to happen in?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A strict chain: sign a lease, get the landlord's Wohnungsgeberbestätigung, do the Anmeldung, open the Sparkasse account, then set up the deposit account. The Anmeldung certificate is also what the school will ask for.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Back to school: for the Haidhausen addresses we're looking at, the catchment school is the Grundschule an der Kirchenstraße.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a well-regarded school, and a short walk from most of Haidhausen.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sofia still prefers the international school, so Lia doesn't have to struggle with German. I worry about the €18,000 a year.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Both worries are fair. The fees [N_17] add up over years, while a Grundschule gives Lia German and local friends, which matters if you stay long-term.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We've decided: Kirchenstraße, plus a weekly German tutor so Lia catches up faster.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A good compromise: free, local, and the tutor addresses Sofia's concern.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How do we register her at the school?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: In person at the school, with Lia's documents and proof of address.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What counts as proof of address?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The Anmeldung certificate, so school registration sits at the end of the same chain [N_33]: lease, landlord form, Anmeldung, then the school.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Insurance again: Sofia has an interview with a Munich design studio next week. She's starting to think a local job would be better than working remotely for Lisbon.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That would change a few things, insurance included.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Would she still be co-insured on my TK policy if she works in Munich?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Let's check the co-insurance rules for employed spouses.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What are the rules?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Co-insurance only covers family members without a significant income. If Sofia takes a salaried job in Munich, she'll be insured through her own employer. Lia stays co-insured on your policy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Moving logistics: should we bring our car or sell it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Importing a car means German registration and possibly an inspection. Let's get a moving quote first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: For the household goods, Transeuropa Movers can do a full 20 ft container. Let's book that.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: A full container fits the furniture and, in principle, the car. Booked with Transeuropa.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The Blue Card pre-approval arrived. The KVR appointment is still 8 July, though.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good; with the pre-approval your entry visa is straightforward. The 8 July appointment stays.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: To be safe, Brennwerk agreed to move my start date to 15 July, after the appointment.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That removes any doubt about working before the card is issued. Your start date is now 15 July.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Does the later start mess up the temporary flat?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Not really: it still runs until 31 July [N_25], so you'd just use it from mid-July.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I flew over for a weekend and viewed three Haidhausen flats.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good; viewings in person make a huge difference with Munich landlords.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We got one! Lease signed: €2,480 warm, starting 1 August.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations. €2,480 is within your €2,600 cap, and a 1 August start means you no longer depend on the temporary flat after July.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So the temporary flat is only needed from 15 to 31 July now?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Right: with the later start [N_45], you'll use it for just over two weeks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We've arrived in Munich! The new landlord already gave us the Wohnungsgeberbestätigung for the Haidhausen flat.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Perfect: with that form you can do the Anmeldung for the new address right away, even before moving in on 1 August.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Anmeldung done at the Bürgerbüro this morning!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That unlocks the rest of the chain: bank account, deposit, school registration.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The Sparkasse account is open.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good; that's your main account for rent and the deposit.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the deposit is in the Mietkautionskonto. The landlord confirmed.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then the whole registration and banking chain is complete.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We registered Lia at Kirchenstraße with the Anmeldung certificate.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Great, the last link in the chain.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The school tested Lia's German. As expected, she's a beginner.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Normal for a new arrival. Schools then decide how to place her.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The school wants Lia to start in the Übergangsklasse, a transition class for new arrivals, for about six months, before joining a regular third-grade class. We'll keep the tutor too.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: That's a strong model: intensive German with other newcomers, then a regular class. So the plan is Kirchenstraße, starting in the Übergangsklasse, plus the weekly tutor.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sofia worries it will set Lia back a year.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Usually the opposite: children who get a solid German base first tend to catch up faster in regular classes than those thrown straight in.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Sofia got the job at the Munich design studio!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations to her! That settles the question of working remotely.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She's resigning from the Lisbon agency. No more remote work for them.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Then the plan to keep her Lisbon job is off. She'll be a regular employee in Munich from September.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What happens with insurance now?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: As we worked out [N_41]: from her start date Sofia is insured through her new employer, and Lia stays co-insured on your TK policy.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Transeuropa's final quote for the full 20 ft container, car included, is €7,800. That's way over what we planned.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The car is the expensive part: it takes most of the container space and needs German registration afterwards.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Haidhausen has great transport and we'd hardly use a car. Let's sell it and ship the rest in a shared container.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Agreed: sell the car in Lisbon and switch to a shared container for the household goods. Much cheaper, and it arrives in a similar time.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The KVR issued my Blue Card, and Sofia's residence permit came with it.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Congratulations, that's the legal side done for both of you.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We moved into the Haidhausen flat yesterday.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Welcome home! Mostly empty for now, I assume, until the container arrives.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Yes, when does our stuff arrive?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Shared containers usually take a little longer to fill; Transeuropa's estimate is the first week of August.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The container arrived today and everything was unloaded.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Great timing, well before school starts.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: One box is missing: the one with Lia's books.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Check the inventory list the movers made at packing; each box should be numbered.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Should we file an insurance claim?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Report it to Transeuropa in writing first; the transit insurance usually requires notice within a few days of delivery.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Transeuropa found the box: it had been loaded onto another family's shipment. It's being delivered next week.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Good outcome. Keep the written report until it arrives.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you give me the status of everything?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Visa: Blue Card issued. Housing: in Haidhausen at €2,480. Registration and bank: Anmeldung, Sparkasse and deposit done. School: Lia starts at Kirchenstraße in the transition class. Insurance: TK for you and Lia, Sofia through her employer. Moving: goods arrived, car sold.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's still open?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Three admin items: waiting for your tax ID, the broadcasting fee registration, and sorting out transport now that you have no car.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Lia's school confirmed her first day: 14 September.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Perfect, with a few weeks to settle in first.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Has the tax ID shown up? Brennwerk payroll keeps asking.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: It's sent automatically by post a few weeks after the Anmeldung, so it should arrive soon.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: It arrived today!

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Send it to Brennwerk's payroll so your salary is taxed correctly from the start.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: We got a letter about the Rundfunkbeitrag. What is it?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: The public broadcasting fee: every household pays it, whether or not you own a TV.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How much, and do we both pay?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Once per household, not per person: roughly €18 a month. Register the household once, in one name.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Without a car, what's the best way to get around?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Munich's public transport covers everything you need from Haidhausen. Now that the car is sold [N_62], a monthly Deutschlandticket is the obvious choice.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Brennwerk subsidises the Deutschlandticket as a job ticket, so I've ordered it through them.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Even better. That closes the last open item.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Looking back, what changed from our April plan?

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: Five things: Haidhausen instead of Pasing [N_28]; Sparkasse instead of N26 as the main bank [N_32]; a 15 July start instead of 1 July [N_45]; Sofia working in Munich instead of remotely for Lisbon [N_59]; and selling the car with a shared container instead of shipping everything [N_62].

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Tomorrow Sofia starts her new job, and in two weeks Lia starts school. I think we're actually settled.

turns.speaker: assistant
turns.text: You are: permits, home, bank, insurance, school and work all in place before the school year. Congratulations to all three of you.
